title: Binance says fake job interview led to $6.3 billion crypto heist
content_md: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance says North Korean hackers used a fake job interview to trick an employee into installing malware that ultimately let them compromise the company's wallet infrastructure and steal about $6.34 billion in digital assets. This new information was shared in an incident report published today, which details how the attackers used social engineering, malicious software, and compromised internal systems to carry out the October 29 crypto theft. As previously reported by BleepingComputer, the FBI attributed the attack to North Korean state-sponsored hackers known as TraderTraitor, also tracked as Lazarus Group, Jade Sleet, and APT38. Binance says the attack began in September when a software engineer was contacted through a legitimate job-hunting platform by someone impersonating a Project Director at a fictitious company. The employee's profile referenced his experience at Binance, making him a valuable target for attackers looking to breach the cryptocurrency exchange. The fake recruiter scheduled two interviews for the employee, first with someone posing as a human resources representative, then with another individual claiming to be the company's CEO. During the first interview, the fake HR representative held a live video call and shared a social media account with personal photos and videos to build trust.
